LESSON: NAMING

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.6: Naming

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Naming. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Name objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment.
2. Take pleasure in naming objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment. 19 reference to objects in the environment. identifying colours in the immediate environment. walk and encouraged to identify colours. vocabulary games and encouraged to use new words by integrating them their child play and daily experiences, and naturally weaving them in and out of conversations with learners. viewing video clips or animation to help them connect words with meaning.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Name objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to name objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Take pleasure in naming objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment. 19 reference to objects in the environment. identifying colours in the immediate environment. walk and encouraged to identify colours. vocabulary games and encouraged to use new words by integrating them their child play and daily experiences, and naturally weaving them in and out of conversations with learners. viewing video clips or animation to help them connect words with meaning.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to take pleasure in naming objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment. 19 reference to objects in the environment. identifying colours in the immediate environment. walk and encouraged to identify colours. vocabulary games and encouraged to use new words by integrating them their child play and daily experiences, and naturally weaving them in and out of conversations with learners. viewing video clips or animation to help them connect words with meaning. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Naming.
2. Explain Naming to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Naming.
4. Show that you can: Name objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Naming. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Naming important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Name objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment.
2. Take pleasure in naming objects, people, animals and colours in the immediate environment. 19 reference to objects in the environment. identifying colours in the immediate environment. walk and encouraged to identify colours. vocabulary games and encouraged to use new words by integrating them their child play and daily experiences, and naturally weaving them in and out of conversations with learners. viewing video clips or animation to help them connect words with meaning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
